column5: Description

You gain the ability to transmute matter through touch. Target a volume of up to one liter and one kilogram in weight that you can physically separate from its surroundings. After several minutes of focus, the targeted matter glows briefly and transmutes, increasing the atomic number of each element within by exactly one.

The time required scales with the atomic number of the elements involved. Turning iron (26) into cobalt (27), for example, takes approximately twenty minutes of concentration. The transmutation produces stable isotopes whenever possible, though there may be logical, unexpected, or even dangerous consequences, albeit somewhat softened from what physics would normally dictate.

Once you land an initial strike on an opponent, your subsequent attacks against the same target grow increasingly devastating. Each successive blow deals twice the damage of the previous one. For example, if your first hit causes a minor abrasion, the second strike will be twice as severe, and the third strike will be four times as severe as the first.

This escalation resets if you switch targets and rapidly decays, if you pause between attacks for too long. The ability only functions if your first attack deals meaningful damage. It doesn't work if your first attack didn't deal enough damage and can the effect can be interrupted by other exotic effects.

You can use metaphorical sources of flame inside and around you to fuel your magic. For example, you can draw upon your own flaming rage or fires of will to produce mystical effects. Doing so will make these inner fires burn brighter for a time, but they will also turn to cold ash more quickly. This means that if you use something like rage or willpower as fuel, they will temporarily intensify, only to burn out afterward - leaving behind disinterest, apathy, or similar emotional numbness. You will need to restore them before they can be used again. As such, it is often wiser to use something like the potential flames trapped inside gunpowder on your person as fuel, even if such sources may be less effective or nearly impossible to utilize for certain tasks.

Sourcing metaphorical flames requires creativity and careful thought. Some sources are easier or better suited for particular magical tasks than others, and the type of flame you use may influence the resulting magic. For instance, you cannot directly use the flames of another person's rage, but if you bait them into focusing their anger on you, it becomes easier to draw upon. Similarly, using flames of rage is well-suited for violent tasks, though the magic may take on side-effects associated with anger: effects that become much more pronounced if the task already aligns closely with the concept of rage. Not everything can serve as a source; it must be some form of metaphorical flame, or at the very least, fuel for one.

You can create free fire spirits or infuse items with them using living things you have burned down yourself as the source - either from their ashes or by literally dragging specks of "inner fire" from the corpses of your foes. These "fiends" need to eat fire or highly flammable materials to survive, but even then, they have limited and usually short lifespans because they age relatively quickly. They are generally aligned with you, listen to your orders, and are loyal, but tend to be mischievous and "fiery" in character due to their nature. They live longer when infused into objects, but their effects are less powerful in that form. Depending on exotic and unqiue properties of things you burnt to create them, friends might possess some traces of traits and characteristics of the burnt object.

You possess the ability to project and throw small pellets that burst into a cloud of capsaicin-derived substance, similar to tear gas but potentially stronger. You have control over the volume of gas clouds each pellet produces when you create it and the potency of substance. You are immune to the effects of the tear gas in general, allowing you to navigate through the cloud unharmed. Pellets do not persist for long - they disappear after some time, if they lose contact with you and/or not being used/destroyed.

You possess the ability to rapidly grow and produce dead wood from your own body. This wood can take on various shapes such as beams, stakes, thorns, curved branches, and other pointy objects. You have the flexibility to make them hollow or alter their inner structure or surface for a little while, even making them polished. Your power does not tarnish your clothes or other thin materials around you (if you don't want it to). The wood you create is dark, dense, and exceptionally hard. It is resistant to catching fire, but if it does ignite, it burns rapidly. It is very susceptible to natural decay and rots relatively quickly over time.

You have the power to infuse existing or created wood (including alive) with your energy. For instance, you can charge a small piece of wood, throw it, and after a certain time, it will begin to transform into preprogrammed pointed shapes, resembling your own body’s abilities, until the charge is depleted. Alternatively, you can grow wood from other wooden surfaces that you come into contact with. Charged wood, under your control, can be easily broken by you and poses no harm to you.

You have a metaphorical vessel of 'mortis essence' inside your soul. You can replenish this magic by killing or witnessing death personally. You become stronger and can restore powers in places drenched in death or strongly associated with the dead, as recognized by the local population or creatures in the area.

You gain more from killing or witnessing the death of someone who resists death or being killed. You also gain more from sleeping or meditating in places associated with the dead. Different creatures, types of death, and locations influence your replenishment. You cannot accumulate too much mortis essence, as it makes you more vulnerable to death: stopping bleeding takes longer, severe wounds are more likely to cause death, you get ill more easily, etc. So, you need to find a way to get rid of the excess or figure out how to block/control automatic replenishment of the essence before it kills you. Mortis essence is strongly aligned with arts related to death and the dead, such as necromancy or burial arts, but is not limited to them.

When breaking down or disassembling something, you can often find spare parts inside, even if there shouldn't be any. While you cannot precisely control which spare part you will get, you can steer it slightly in the desired direction. Repeatedly disassembling and reassembling objects allows you to dupe pieces with each iteration. Although, there are diminishing returns for doing it to the exact same thing over and over again.

The terms 'disassembly' and 'something' are quite flexible - breaking rocks with a pickaxe or preparing wood also technically count as disassembling. As a result, you may find yourself with more spare parts or useful items than expected, even in these cases. Very rarely, when searching for space parts, you might discover unique, thematic items related to what you disassembled among spare parts - for example, finding a golden nugget in a piece of rock you broke down, even if it shouldn’t be there. You also have a knack for dismantling objects quickly, safely and carefully. Nothing supernatural though.

You can cause almost any physical object or part of it to pop, as if it were a balloon - simply by applying enough pressure or using something like a needle. Larger and more massive objects explode with greater power. After performing the 'pop' action, you have a short window of invulnerability to protect you from the explosion itself and some of the shards it produces, but nothing beyond that. You have perfect control over when this ability is active.

You can unravel matter and energy into thick, colorful threads and wind them into balls that represent aspects of an object. Simply touching your target starts the process. These threads can be stored in a special pocket dimension and accessed at any time. If you haven't altered the threads, you can turn them back into the original objects. The mass, volume, and complexity of the target determine how many threads you obtain and how easy/hard it is to do, but it will always be lesser in mass and volume than the original unraveled object. 

You can split these threads into more, unraveling the nature of the object into simpler aspects. Using different threads, you can create patterns so that when they are reassembled, the resulting object will be different - made of aspects of your original target and inspired by the new shape. You are an expert in working with threads and possess an unnatural intuition for manipulating aspect threads specifically. Others can also work with these threads and even restore them into objects using the right supernatural energies or abilities, but without your unnatural intuition, it is difficult for them to find effective or useful patterns.

You cannot die from overdrinking; at some point, it will stop worsening. Any damage caused by drinking will be healed by a short hangover afterward. You do not suffer from the usual side effects of alcoholism, such as developing a tolerance to alcohol. While you are at least a little bit drunk, you cannot be poisoned by other substances. Your luck slightly increases with how drunk you are at the moment, though there is a limit. You are extremely knowledgeable about cocktails, alcoholic beverages, and how to drink them correctly. 

You can consume methanol or similar "alcoholic" substances without dying, going blind, or experiencing other severe consequences, but the hangover will be longer and much worse. You can still get drunk, even if other powers prohibit or make it impossible. You can experience degrees of drunkenness beyond what an unmodified human brain can normally comprehend. If you want to get intoxicated from drinking at the moment - you will!

You can instantly conjure great quantities of fresh, boiling-hot (or cold, depending on the dish), and delicious soup, broth or stew in any targeted empty vessel. It must be some kind of mundane soup, broth or stew, and you should be somewhat familiar with specific dish to actually summon it. 

The substance created this way is enhanced to be perpetually hot (or cold, depending on the dish) and fresh until eaten or ruined by external factors (like dirt getting into it). After that, these special properties gradually (or abruptly) diminish and disappear completely. You can instantly fill a cauldron with your favorite stew, definitely a tub, or even the whole room. It just needs to be some non-living vessel with physical access to its insides. There is a limit of how much you can create at once, but its a lot of stew/soup/broth.

This metaperk automatically connects to all other perks and powers you have and updates when you acquire new ones. Its primary goal is the management and control of the various effects that powers give you. It grants you the ability to tune and even turn powers on or off, even for ones which usually don't have any means of control. You can preprogram various quick changes to tweak the operation of many abilities at once, giving you more precise control over the abilities you possess and making it easier to monitor what they do and when. Of course, it works a bit differently with different perks and tries to adapt to them. Basically, it just gives a control panel to better monitor and manage your powers.

You are capable of absorbing light with the surface of your body, turning it into a transparent fluid and excreting it from any point on your body. Disturbing this substance causes it to partly revert back into light (for example, by suddenly heating it or punching it hard). This liquid is practically weightless and has very low viscosity. However, you can concentrate more light into the same volume of liquid. Doing so will make it heavier and more viscous, the more light you pack into it. Additionally, disturbing it will produce brighter light with a shorter wavelength. You are good at absorbing visible light but terrible at absorbing non-visible light. There is a limit to how much you can absorb, store, and recycle per unit of time.

You have an inventory space size of one cubic meter. You can put resources, materials, and even some components into this extradimensional space with a touch, as long as they are not larger than a cube with a side of one meter. Things inside this space will be converted from one resource into another after specific time passes. How long this takes depends on three parameters: Properties, Composition, and Shape. How different these three between the original target and intended result. For example, you can put one type of steel into this space and turn it into another of your liking in a matter of minutes: one alloy of iron transformed into another. 

You are only aware of how long the transformation will take after putting something inside the space and choosing end state of conversion. You can eject items at any time (they will remain unchanged if not enough time has passed for full processing) and must do so if you want to change what is currently contained in this cubic dimension (you cannot add stuff, while something is inside). Trying to turn something into a completely different type of entity might take years and even decades to process, which is usually not worth it. Some small amount of material gets lost in the conversion process, proportionally to how much time it took to convert. End result depends on what you are asking this power to do, but cannot be anything but resource, material or component.

Valaknots are ancient symbols that warp body and mind when carved into flesh. Believed to be gifted to mortals by the god of change, Maudamouros, these symbols allow the manipulation of living creatures - including animals, plants, and fungi. Valaknots do not work on dead material; they require living entities. They can reshape bodies, empowering or diminishing them in countless ways, and can even grant some the power to conjure or manipulate different matter. Valaknots are arranged into patterns called Valachains. Mistakes in carving will lead to consequences. 

You have the expertise and carving skills of a decently experienced Valaknot practitioner, but without a specific focus or tradition. You possess your own rather humble mental library of randomly chosen Valaknots: you know what they do and how they mesh together into various Valachains. By spending additional 200 CP (or more), you can buy proficiency in one of the specific traditions of the art: The Flesh Forge, The Saltfen Brood, The Fellwood Druids. By personally instructing and guiding others, you might give them ability to use and teach others the art of Valaknots. (Author: Creature Guild)

You gain the ability to psychically manipulate holes. By touching the tangible edge of any opening, you can stretch or compress it temporarily, though you cannot permanently change its size. You can also pluck a hole from its location and fling it as a projectile; upon impact, it re-opens to its original dimensions. Crucially, when you remove a hole, you can preserve its "destination," allowing you to relocate an entrance while keeping it connected to its original exit. 

By touching the edges in sequence, you can link multiple holes to create a portal network, which you can dismiss as long as you are near one terminus. Passing objects through a chain of linked holes of different sizes/shapes will resize or deform them accordingly (process doesn't create/destroy matter). Finally, you can turn a removed hole inside out to create an unstable "anti-hole." This substance acts as a perfect, repulsive barrier, but it will explosively expand and disappear unless you are nearby to stabilize it.

You are a genius of toxicity and a pioneer of chemical warfare. You possess an innate resistance to harmful agents, able to build total immunity through exposure, and the expertise to design, deploy, and counter modern Earth chemical weapons. Your talent borders on the supernatural, allowing you to invent new poisons with ease. 

This path has also granted you mastery over a unique necromancy, letting you animate organic chemical weapons - such as giving sentience to clouds of poison gas that can puppet the corpses of the fallen. Through alchemical sigils and artifacts, you can extract and command toxins with precision. Furthermore, you may initiate students into this art through ritual and tutelage, though their mastery will depend on their own aptitude and your guidance.

You can fire a beam of light that petrifies living creatures for up to a year. The beam's speed can vary from a bullet to a falling feather. Petrified creatures are alive but in a soul-slumber, unable to sense or do anything. Resistance to this effect varies based on size, abilities, properties or armor the target possess. You are an excellent sculptor and can use this skill on your statues: any carving or modification you make will heal, damage, or permanently reshape the creature when they revert. Furthermore, you can animate these statues as obedient servants. They retain their original skills and abilities, possess the durability and weight of stone, and are proportionally stronger. However, they don't have ego, cannot grow and need renewing orders to act in effective way.

You can brew alcohol from virtually anything: rocks, energy fields, or stranger things - as long as you can find a method to work with them. You are a skilled brewer and vintner with expertise in tool creation and farming, guided by an intuition that hints at the probable properties of your creations and potential ways to obtain them. Your brews gain special effects based on their ingredients. You are also highly resistant to poison and the negative effects of intoxicants. When drunk, you gain a healing factor and a notable boost to all physical stats.

Your capacity for invention and research scales directly with your mental instability and psychological suffering. The greater your madness, the greater your scientific genius. Your madness also mildly enhances your ability to avoid danger, improvise, and commit violence. Different mental conditions grant different boons: psychosis might fuel impossible mad scientist contraptions, while other issues aid different pursuits. 

Your psyche possesses an uncanny resilience, slowly healing over time to its baseline state when you took this perk, though this does not erase memories. You can even recover from eldritch truths, though it will be neither pleasant nor quick. Your creations vary in nature; some are blackboxed and impossible to replicate, while others are fully reproducible, albeit with complications.

You gain the intuitive ability to interact with all matter as if it were glass. This versatile power lets you: shatter the strongest stones like fragile glass; walk on water as if it were a solid floor; see through walls as if they were clear windows; reflect light with a piece of wood as if it were a perfect mirror; filter or focus light using a pebble as a lens; and cut flesh with a plastic knife as if its edge were razor-sharp volcanic glass. Mastery of this ability requires time, practice, and imagination to discover its full range of applications.

You can condense almost anything within a small radius around you, including more abstract thingd like light, vacuum, or even fear. If it exists in your radius, you can target it. Before condensing, you gain a vague sense of how dangerous the process might be, though this offers no protection against your own foolishness. The resulting condensates form unique types of matter with special properties, effects, and varying stability. 

You can steer the condensation process with your will, allowing the same source material to yield slightly different results depending on your intentions. It's a case by case thing. Although, there is a limit of how much you can condense at a time, until you find some suitable sources of magic to power this ability in more reliably way, rather than fiat backing.

You can crystallize almost anything within a small radius around you, including more abstract targets like smell, mana, or coldness. If it exists in your radius, you can target it. The resulting crystals form unique types of matter with special properties and varying stability. 

Before crystallizing, you gain a vague sense of potential dangers, though this offers no protection against your own foolishness. You can steer the process with your will, allowing the same source material to yield slightly different crystalline results depending on your intent. Although, there is a limit of how much you can crystallize at a time, until you find some suitable sources of magic to power this ability in more reliably way, rather than fiat backing.

You are protected by a perfect, automatic conceptual Repulsion. This passive defence constantly repels anything that would harm you, from physical attacks and poison to exhaustion and even starvation. You can instinctively sense what is being repulsed and how at any given moment. You can slightly modulate this passive defence, but cannot turn off or fully control it.

Furthermore, you can learn to actively wield this power. By perceiving a target and performing the right "mental gymnastics," you can actively repulse specific things (matter, energy, fatigue, or even curses) in controlled bursts. However, active use requires intense focus, is difficult to maintain, and is always weaker than your perfect passive defence (meaning you can never use it to harm yourself) and you must learn from passive Repulsion effect first to achieve anything.

Remember, repulsed things don't vanish; they are simply pushed somewhere else. A repulsed poison might be forced into the ground. There are also many ways to use Repulsion on any given target. For example, pushing space can produce different results, depending on your way of thinking and the situation. 

Only few divine, deeply eldritch or conceptual effects might pierce your Repulsion.

You possess a pool of energy that gradually recharges over 12 hours, which you can spend to apply game-like magical effects to items. Think of Diablo or MMO-style kinds of effects. The enchantments produced are mostly random, though you can slightly steer the result or invest more energy for greater predictability. You don't know possible effects from the start - you need to use the power and see them for yourself. 

Be warned: enchanting an item multiple times is difficult. Stacking too many effects risks erasing previous enchantments, corrupting the item, or warping it entirely. It is much easier and more efficient to apply this effect to small items or equipment, and much harder to focus it on consumables, architecture or generally big thing. Your energy pool slowly grows over time, but only if you regularly and completely exhaust it.

You can activate this power, causing your eyes to shine like brilliant gemstones. When you focus on an object, the ability scans it to trace its ontological origin, determining how "fake" it is and what it is trying to emulate.

This allows you to accurately distinguish forged documents from authentic ones, identify counterfeit goods, and recognize clones of creatures for what they are. The power does not tell you if the fake is better or worse than the original, nor does it reveal exactly how it is fake - only what it attempts to emulate and whether it is, in fact, a fake. The scanning process requires some time of concentration to reach a conclusion.

You possess an impeccable understanding of social conduct. You instinctively know the basic rules, customs, and protocols required for polite and respectful behavior in practically any culture you encounter, from street gangs to high society, warrior clans to merchant guilds, allowing you to navigate any interaction without embarrassing yourself or committing a social faux pas.

This perk functions on two levels. First, it provides you with practical knowledge of common and historical etiquette systems for most situations and groups on Earth. Second, it grants you an enhanced intuition that allows you to decipher and adapt to entirely new systems of etiquette with minimal exposure, simply by observing and interacting with the group in question.

You possess the ability to traverse dimensions beyond the merely physical. You can open, close, and navigate paths through space and time, but also through realms not associated with them. Enter mental planes, the dimension of pure mathematics, or specific afterlives, and even bring things back from one dimension to another. However, your ability to find and reach a destination depends on your understanding and conceptualization of the target.

This power also grants a passive effect: perfect evasion. When something is about to strike you, this defense will shift part of your existence (body, soul, mind, or whatever) into another dimension, safely and efficiently dodging the incoming doom. These moments of evasion also offer rare opportunities to grasp tiny specks of enlightenment, deepening your understanding for future active use of this Authority. But at the beginning you can be sure: you being would never be in the path of the incoming attack.

Only few divine, deeply eldritch or conceptual effects might counter your passive evasion.

You gain the ability to summon a swarm of dozens to hundreds of invisible piranhas that swim through the air as if it were water. The piranhas are entirely intangible constructs of power (not real creatures) but their razor-sharp teeth are very real to anything they bite. Invisible to the eye, the swarm can only be detected by the chilling sound of countless tiny jaws gnashing together as they descend upon your foes. The swarm obeys your mental commands, relentlessly harassing, distracting, and shredding anything in their path until dismissed or getting too far from you.

Your magic is derived from the power held within your soul, generating whatever fuel is necessary internally without external help. However, this connection cuts both ways. Because you power all miracles and effects entirely by yourself, there is a hard limit to what your soul (or any mortal soul) can fuel before suffering consequences: overdrawing can lead to soul fatigue, soul warping and damage, or worse. Furthermore, with your magic so directly tethered to your essence, skilled enemies or supernatural entities may be able to track, exploit, or even attack you through this connection if they know how to follow the line back to its source.

Your magic is written in the heavens, drawing power from astrological signs, celestial alignments, and the portents written in the night sky. When the stars are right, your spells swell with incredible potency, and you can read the firmament to cast rituals keyed to specific constellations. However, this connection to the cosmos is not without risk. You are bound to the sky's whims - during celestial absences, opposing signs, or when the stars are "wrong," your power wanes significantly or becomes unpredictable.

Your magic is not drawn from incantations or reagents, but from the raw, unyielding strength of your mind. High emotions (rage, grief, ecstasy, or pure determination) serve as fuel for your spells, allowing you to shape phenomena through sheer force of will. A disciplined mind can achieve miracles that leave conventional casters baffled. 

However, this dependence on your mental state creates significant vulnerabilities. Strong emotional suppression leaves you powerless, while intense feelings can cause your magic to flare uncontrollably or twist to reflect your mood. Moreover, because your spells are extensions of your psyche, mental attacks, psychic feedback, or emotional manipulation can directly disrupt your casting or even turn your own power against you.

Your magic is fueled directly by your own life force, drawn from your health, vitality, and physical well-being. This allows you to cast spells without any external components or mana pools - your body itself becomes the battery, capable of producing miraculous effects through sheer sacrifice. 

Unfortunetly, this power extracts a heavy toll. Every spell leaves you weaker, sicker, and closer to collapse; overcasting can induce wasting sickness, temporary crippling, or even threaten your life if you push too far. Moreover, because your magic is literally part of your living flesh, healers and life-sensing entities can detect your condition at a glance, and any drain or damage to your body directly impacts your ability to cast until you recover.

Your magic draws on natural wellsprings like leylines to fuel itself, granting you tremendous power when connected to such sources, but only situationally. This principle transcends the existence of magic itself. Even in worlds without ambient enchantment, dead zones, or technological realities, you can still draw power from natural features that approximate leylines: continental fault lines, river confluences, ancient migration paths, or geomagnetic anomalies. Any place where the world itself holds concentrated natural energy becomes a wellspring for your magic. 

However, you remain bound by geography and vulnerability - away from such sites your power fades, and those attuned to the land (druids, earth spirits, or even geologists with supernatural sensitivity) can sense your tapping and may object to your presence.

Your magic reaches beyond reality, drawing power from alternate dimensions to fuel your spells. Each type of effect (fire, shadow, time, force) can be sourced from a different reality, granting you incredible versatility and access to energies no single world could provide. By pulling from dimensions with exotic physical laws, your magic can achieve effects that seem impossible by local standards. 

However, every spell opens a temporary bridge, and attention flows both ways. Prolonged casting, reckless draws, or using the same dimension too frequently can attract the notice of things that dwell within - hunger entities, conceptual predators, or entire ecologies that view your magic as an invasion. Worse, if a connection is forced or held too long, something may follow the current back.

Your magic flows not from within, but through the will of a patron you have bargained with. This entity channels its power directly to you, granting access to spells and abilities far beyond your natural capacity - and if you choose wisely, that patron may very well take the form of your own familiar, a companion always at your side. 

However, you are never truly casting alone. Your patron can choose to withhold, distort, or amplify your magic based on your alignment with their interests, and every spell you cast announces your connection to them. Those versed in the occult can trace your power back to its source, potentially targeting your patron or exploiting the link. Moreover, the bargain cuts both ways - if your patron is harmed, bound, or banished, your magic goes with them until they are freed.

Your magic is fueled not by energy, but by revelation - you must offer secrets to power your spells. Every casting consumes a piece of hidden knowledge: a personal shame, a confidential plan, the true name of a distant star, or the location of a buried treasure. The greater the secret's worth (its intimacy, its potential to harm if revealed, its significance to the world) the more powerful the effect you can conjure. This allows you to work magic far beyond conventional limits, trading information for miracles. 

Unfortunetly, secrets spent are truly gone, ripped from your memory and sometimes even from reality nearby, made harder for you to rediscover and remeber. Those who once trusted you may sense something missing, diviners can detect the gaps where knowledge used to be, and beings who hoard secrets (librarians of forbidden lore, elder gods, or simply the very paranoid) will take great interest in someone who burns information as fuel.

Your magic is powered not by external forces, but by the weight of your own sworn word. By placing binding restrictions upon yourself (vows of poverty, silence, non-violence, or any self-imposed limitation) you generate power proportional to the difficulty and sincerity of the oath. The greater the sacrifice of freedom, the mightier the magic you can fuel. This allows you to achieve remarkable effects simply by denying yourself options that others take for granted. 

Of course, oaths are not to be broken lightly. Violating a sworn restriction doesn't just cost you power - it can shatter your connection for a long period of time, inflict backlash upon your mind or body, and you never know true consequences beforehand. Moreover, those who can detect or manipulate promises (celestial scribes, devilish contractors, or feigned lords) may attempt to exploit your bonds, and every vow you take creates a thread others might one day pull.

Belief itself becomes fuel for your magic. The convictions of others (whether organized religion, local superstitions, cultural myths, or simple misunderstandings) generate power that you can channel into supernatural effects. A town's fervent belief in a local saint lets you work healing; widespread terror of a monster allows you to summon shadows; a misconception about haunted ground grants you power over the dead. The stronger and more widespread the belief, the mightier the miracle you can perform. 

Of course, you are bound by the content of that belief. You cannot easily contradict the source of your power - a miracle drawn from fear will feel terrible, one drawn from love will feel gentle, and attempting to use belief against its nature may cause the magic to fail or twist unexpectedly. Moreover, those who shape belief (priests, tyrants, memetic threats) can starve or poison your fuel source, and you may find yourself unconsciously reinforcing the very misconceptions you rely upon to maintain your power.

Your magic operates on verifiable principles. By studying the universe as a logical system of natural laws, you derive spellcraft from formula rather than faith or bloodline. This grants you exceptional stability - your workings are rooted in reality, making them difficult to disrupt or counterspell. You gain a natural talent for learning and reverse-engineering any supernatural phenomenon you encounter.

However, this framework is a model, not a window. Encountering truly alien or paradoxical phenomena that contradict your established understanding can cause your magic to falter or produce unexpected results until you painstakingly update your theories and system of thought.

You derive your power from consumed elixirs and alchemical creations, brewed through a rigid system of rules and philosophy. These concoctions provide the necessary fuel to cast, with effects determined by the precision of your art. Potions can be prepared in advance, allowing for tactical flexibility, but your capabilities are limited by your stock, supplies and preparation. The strict formulae required mean innovation is slow and methodical (trial and error has real consequences) and some things just cannot be done withing the system you use. It's not all-encompassing.

Your magic is channeled through a specific tool: a wand, blade, crystal, or other focused implement (choose one; cannot be overly broad definition). This focus grants you inherent talent and refined skill in casting through your chosen instrument, with your magic adapted to utilize it effectively by the perk. Loss or destruction of your implement leaves you severely hampered until it is recovered or replaced. Should you find yourself without any magic to channel currently, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your magic is worked through formal rites: circles, sacrifices, and structured ceremonies. Choose an aesthetic style or specific real-world occult system; your magic will be perfectly adapted to implement this practice. Rituals allow for potent, versatile effects but require time, preparation, and proper conditions. You gain innate talent and skill in these methods. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your magic is activated and shaped by consuming specific substances: potions, rare metals, alchemical herbs, or similar (choose some focused category). These consumables act as both fuel and focus, allowing you to draw out and enhance your abilities. Your magic is perfectly adapted to this practice, granting you innate talent in preparing and utilizing your chosen materials. Without your consumables, your power is severely limited. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your magic is enacted through spoken words, incantations, or symbolic utterance. Choose a specific language, runic system, or form of chant/music (cannot be overly broad). Your magic is perfectly adapted to this practice, with power and precision tied to your diction, understanding and delivery. You gain innate talent and skill in these methods. Silencing or impeding your speech severely hampers your casting. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your magic is channeled through somatic motion: hand signs, martial forms, dance, or precise gestures. Choose some specific style or theme for your practice (cannot be overly broad). Your power is perfectly adapted to this practice, with complex effects requiring correspondingly intricate movements. You gain innate talent and skill in these methods. Restraint or immobilization leaves you severely hampered. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your magic is channeled through trophies: body parts or significant possessions taken from defeated foes. These anchors allow you to draw out, control, and reliably shape your power, with effects often influenced by the nature of your defeated enemy. Your magic is perfectly adapted to this practice, granting innate talent in harvesting, preparing, and utilizing trophies. Without sufficient anchors, your power becomes diffuse and difficult to control. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your magic manifests with unavoidable visual phenomena: motes of light, floating symbols, energy corona, or similar displays. Attempting to suppress these effects weakens, destabilizes, or alters your intended outcome; your practice is inherently a form of self-expression. You gain innate talent and skill in these methods, with your magic perfectly adapted to this aesthetic. Stealth casting is nearly impossible without accepting significant penalties. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your power is distributed across multiple totems - each dedicated charm, fetish, or focus enhancing a specific category of ability rather than serving as a single casting implement. You gain innate talent and skill in creating and utilizing these totems, with your magic perfectly adapted to this practice. Losing a totem weakens access to that aspect of your power until it is recovered or replaced. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your enchanting centers around a dedicated power source (a gemstone, crystal, or similar focus) that is set into an object to grant it magical properties. The focus determines the enchantment's capacity and nature, while the object shapes its application. You gain innate talent in preparing, cutting, and setting these focal points. Without a suitable focus, your ability to create enchanted items is severely limited. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your enchanted creations take the form of intricate mechanical devices: systems of gears, pistons, and housings that appear purely technological but are fundamentally magical in operation. This aesthetic is intrinsic to your craft; attempts to create enchantments with a different appearance prove difficult or unstable. You gain innate talent in designing and constructing these magical machines. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your enchantments are worked through the inscription of runes, glyphs, or symbolic marks upon objects. Each symbol carries specific properties, with complex enchantments requiring layered or interlocking designs. You gain innate talent in carving, painting, or otherwise applying these symbols effectively. Damage to the inscribed markings weakens or disrupts the enchantment until repaired. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your enchanting requires channeling power through a physical filter (a crystal, lens, or similar medium) which shapes and refines raw magic into stable enchantments. The filter's quality and properties influence the resulting enchantment's characteristics. You gain innate talent in selecting and utilizing appropriate filters for your purposes. Without a suitable filter, your ability to enchant is severely hampered. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your enchanting produces small devices that project temporary magical constructs: tools, weapons, or effects that manifest for limited duration. Multiple templates can be stored within a single object and cycled as needed, but none can be maintained indefinitely. You gain innate talent in creating and storing these projection patterns. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your enchanting works through gradual saturation - slowly infusing magic into an existing object until it becomes permanently enchanted. The process takes time proportional to the desired power and the object's resistance to accepting magic. You gain innate talent in sensing an object's capacity and guiding the infusion safely. Interrupting the process can damage or destabilize the object. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your enchantments are woven into items during their mundane creation: forging, carving, weaving, or similar craft processes. The final enchantment's quality depends on both your magical skill and the physical craftsmanship of the object itself. You gain innate talent in integrating spellwork seamlessly into traditional making. Post-creation attempts to enchant are significantly more difficult. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your enchanting binds spirits within objects: trapping, planting, or populating them to fuel magical properties. The spirit's nature and disposition shape the resulting enchantment's character and behavior. You gain innate talent in attracting, negotiating with, or compelling spirits into vessels. Spirits may eventually fade, escape, or require appeasement. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your items grow in power through legendary use - great deeds performed with them shape and strengthen their enchantments. Before an item can accumulate power, you must first imbue it with a specific purpose, attuning it to certain actions while disattuning it from others. Power builds gradually with each significant deed, eventually reaching a peak where the enchantment stabilizes and ceases to grow. You gain innate talent in setting purposes and guiding an item's legend. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your items absorb power through sustained use in religious ceremonies: rituals, offerings, and devotions gradually imbuing them with properties tied to those beliefs and practices. The longer an item is employed in worship, the stronger and more refined its enchantment becomes. You gain innate talent in conducting ceremonies and guiding an item's spiritual saturation. Items removed from their religious context may slowly fade or require renewal. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your wards are anchored to a single large diagram or magic circle, which dictates the ward's properties, boundaries, and behavior. The precision and complexity of the diagram determine the ward's sophistication and power. You gain innate talent in designing, inscribing, and activating these ward circles. Damaging the diagram disrupts or collapses the ward entirely until repaired. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your wards are anchored to a central object (a wardstone, crystal, or similar focus) that controls and maintains the protective barrier. Destroying or removing this object collapses the entire ward network. You gain innate talent in creating, placing, and attuning these wardstones to specific defenses. Multiple stones can be linked for larger or more complex ward systems. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your wards require physical markers or tags placed around the protected perimeter: carved stones, inscribed stakes, hanging charms, or similar boundary markers. Each tag contributes to the overall ward, and the integrity of the circle depends on all markers remaining in place. You gain innate talent in creating, empowering, and positioning these territorial tags. A single missing or damaged tag creates a gap in your defenses. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your wards are maintained through repeated ritual performance: each ceremony reinforcing, adjusting, or re-powering the protective barriers. The ritual's form directly shapes the ward's properties, allowing you to easily alter workings to change functionality. You gain innate talent in designing and conducting these warding rituals. Neglecting the required ceremonies causes wards to gradually weaken and eventually fail. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your wards are anchored to your personal presence rather than any physical object or marker. So long as you remain within the protected area, the wards maintain themselves at full strength. Leaving the location causes them to gradually weaken and eventually degrade entirely. You gain innate talent in instinctively extending and shaping your presence into protective barriers. Returning after absence requires time for wards to rebuild to full potency. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your wards are living guardians: spirits and beings bound by pact to protect your territory. The nature of their protection depends entirely on the bargains struck, offerings made, and bindings established. You gain innate talent in negotiating with otherworldly entities and securing their service. Guardians require ongoing payment or appeasement; neglected bargains lead to withdrawn protection or active betrayal. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Your wards are created by establishing literal physical barriers: from simple chalk lines to constructed walls. The barrier's quality, scale, and effectiveness at separating spaces directly determines the ward's strength, versatility, and duration. A more substantial, durable wall creates a more powerful, longer-lasting ward. You gain innate talent in integrating magical protection into physical boundaries. The ward only exists where the physical barrier exists; gaps create vulnerabilities. If you currently lack any magical ability, you may re-roll this perk for free.

Charms are a branch of magic that focus on adding magical qualities to targets. Charms are some of the most commonly used spells in a witch or wizard's everyday life, and cover many general utility spells such as levitating objects, breathing underwater, creating or altering light and sounds, erasing memories, or crafting magic items. While this school of magic has a high level of utility, it is not usable in fighting for anyone but the most quick thinking and imaginative. Even then, its spells tend to be less efficient than dedicated curses or hexes. Most non-violent spells are referred to as charms, though not all of them fall under this affinity, such as combat spells like shields or transfigurations.

You have a specialized affinity for physical charms. These spells are able to levitate and manipulate objects, create visual effects, unlock doors, clean areas, fix broken things, and more. These tend to be quality-of-life spells, but do not tend to be very long lasting unless used in enchanting. Semi-useful in combat.

You have a further affinity for mental charms. These spells read or alter a target's mental state. Memory charms, adding minds to magic objects, confounding others, or altering moods. This field is the primary reason the wizarding world has managed to remain a secret for so long. Also includes legilimency.

You have a greater affinity for enchanting, the practice of layering charms on an object to create magic items. Used in wand creation, broom crafting, and magical inventions. This magic can last for millennia. What you can create with this field of magic is heavily influenced by what other magics you know.

Defense Against the Dark Arts. A field dedicated to defending against and combating dangerous magical creatures, effects, and wizards. This field is comprised of many defensive and offensive spells, including shields, hexes, jinxes, and curses. This is an absolute must for anyone looking to fight seriously against the powerful creatures and criminals of the wizarding world. This field also has the most overlap with other affinities, as most spells can be twisted for use in combat by those with a strong imagination. D.A.D.A incorporates some knowledge of the dark arts in an effort to counter them. It also benefits immensely from the strong knowledge of magical creatures and their weaknesses granted by a magical creature affinity.

You have a specialized affinity for offensive abilities; curses, hexes, jinxes, and anything that will damage an opponent. This can overlap with other magic types, such as using charms to drown an enemy or transfiguration to turn them into an animal. This will not protect you from being harmed yourself, however.

You have a specialized affinity for defensive abilities; counter spells, shields, curse breaking, and more. This can extend to other types of magic, such as creating smoke screens or blocking mental intrusions, as well as employing a variety of magics to heal yourself and others of curses and harmful effects.

A dark temptation for many, you have a specialized affinity for the dark arts. These are powerful and dangerous practices that exist for practically every field. The dark arts are more powerful than other types of magic, but are illegal, often deeply immoral, and it is difficult to find useful resources to learn them from.

Transfiguration is the field of magic dedicated to altering the physical elements of the world. In its most basic form, this field allows users to transform one thing into another, such as turning a cup into a bird, switching traits between creatures, or changing the environment. Transfiguration typically involves conjuring or vanishing materials, or a mix of both practices when altering a target. This magic is more scientific than most fields, and requires a complex understanding of the materials being manipulated in order to be used effectively. Most of the changes in this field are temporary, and there are certain restrictions on what can be transfigured. Food, for example, can be summoned and multiplied, but cannot be created from nothing.

You have a specialized affinity for conjuration. This is a branch of transfiguration used to summon something from nothing. This field can even be used to create living creatures, such as snakes, bugs, or birds. This skill has no end to its uses, but objects summoned from thin air tend to be temporary.

You have a specialized affinity for vanishment. This is the practice of removing objects or creatures from existence entirely. Very complicated to use on living creatures, it is typically used to store, reduce, or remove magical and mundane objects. It can also be used for teleportation, such as through the skill of apparition.

Not technically a magic affinity, you have completed a dangerous and complicated ritual to become an animagus. Pick a mundane animal, you can now transform into that animal at will. This can fool some magical defenses and creatures. You are an unregistered animagus, and should fix this or avoid being caught transforming.

You have an affinity for brewing potions. Potions have some of the strongest magical effects of any type of magic, but often require rare or expensive ingredients and a great deal of time to create. Potion making is almost more science than magic, but all potions still require some degree of magical ability to craft. By taking this option, you gain a talent in both alchemy and crafting potions, and may even be able to craft new recipes with time. You can purchase this option second time for half the price (100 CP).

You have an affinity for herbology. This is the study of magical and mundane plants and fungi. Many of these plants produce magically viable ingredients for potion making and enchanting. Studying herbology can assist in collecting these resources and in using the unique and dangerous natures of these plants to your advantage. Taking this affinity will also cut in half the threat posed by magical flora and their byproducts. You can purchase this option second time for half the price (50 CP).

You have an affinity for magical creatures. They are more willing to work with you, and you are twice as effective at understanding how best to interact with them, or fighting them. Care of magical creatures is only an elective, rather than a main course at Hogwarts, meaning this will not necessarily impact your grade. It is a very good skill to have for those trained in defense against the dark arts, however. You can purchase this option second time for half the price (50 CP).

You gain the fully-mastered ability to block the mental intrusions of others. This will allow you to provide false information to mind readers and break free of some mental charms such as the imperius curse. This ability can be learned normally with study and talent, but by taking this option you have mastered the skill from the start.

A trait favored by most Gryffindors, your bravery is legendary. You will never freeze up in combat or during a stressful situation, and have the nerve and self-esteem to ignore peer pressure and threats. You can choose not to dwell too much on past mistakes, and have an almost limitless tolerance for pain.

With Great Valor: You’re a resilient sort, resisting what should be traumatic and making sound decisions even under severe emotional stress. Your conviction remains steady despite public sentiment or even pressure from reputable organisations and institutional authority. You can swiftly take the measure of such groups, seeing corruption, falsehood and injustice for exactly what they are where others choose to look away or be cowed into repeating lies.

The wizarding world tends to be much less serious than that of the non magic community. Now you can contribute to this good humor as well. This greatly improves your creative skills, outside-the-box thinking, and sense of timing and delivery in social and comedic settings. You know how to pull a proper prank, have an instinctive grasp of what you can get away with without taking things too far, and you are never at a loss for words when you decide to exercise your considerable wit.

With Great Valor: You have a talent for capitalising on all manner of failings in your adversaries, and your wit can deftly expose them through devastating ridicule or inspire allies to laugh in the face of terrible odds. You thrive amid chaos; your creativity and aptitude for executing successful pranks also extends to a general talent for sabotage, delicate operations, and small-scale tactics.

You gain the incredible reflexes of a trained auror or quidditch player, as well as the dexterity needed to cast and aim spells reliably in a fight. What's more, these skills will not decline even if you spend your days lazing around during times of peace. Even powerful wizards can lose duels against those with better speed or aim. You will also be naturally talented on a broomstick.

With Great Valor: You don’t just move fast, you think fast. You adapt swiftly and keep exceptional awareness in all manner of high-pressure situations. Even without a plan, you excel at improvising your way out of predicaments, simply acting where others would panic or despair. It only takes a moment to grasp the situation and make a sound decision that would otherwise require a few minutes of careful deliberation.

You have the decisive advantage of emotionally healthy decision-making. This includes the good sense to avoid adopting self-destructive habits or inviting trouble for petty reasons. You see when a choice would ultimately make you unhappy, and are much more likely to overcome personal issues successfully. Even severe problems or lack of support simply mean you need more time and effort.

With Great Loyalty: You’re a reassuring presence, inspiring trust and loyalty while building sound relationships. Your own emotional stability and insight can also help others face their problems and rebuild themselves as happier, stronger people. Even your Rivals are affected – while they’ll still cause you trouble, you can usually keep your relationship closer to healthy competition than an escalation to a lifelong grudge.

You have a natural inclination for winning hearts and influencing others. You can expect to make many friends during your time at Hogwarts, and if you are so inclined could even build a group of loyal followers. As the name suggests, you don't get any practical skills like manipulation or leadership, instead it improves your body language, manners, speech and generally makes you charming.

With Great Loyalty: The sound of your voice can easily captivate a crowd, whether as an informal centre of attention, or when speaking before an audience. In more personal settings, your words give your followers, allies, and comrades strength and hope for a way forward. Diplomacy and fair conduct come naturally to you, making you a natural at managing people or speaking on behalf of a group.

You have something just as useful as natural talent - the dedication needed to study hard. You will find it easy to spend long periods of time reading about, practicing, and studying magic. This also extends to mundane pursuits, practically guaranteeing good grades in classes that don't require magic, like astronomy or history of magic. You will do well on most written tests.

With Great Loyalty: The business of organising people from scratch takes considerable effort. You have an aptitude for this process and its requisite practical skills. Whether administration, logistics and finance, or simply setting fair, effective rules and policy, you know how to keep a group content, cohesive, and running smoothly. This also gives substance and support to your other leadership-related skills and Perks.

You have a natural aptitude for academics. This perk increases your intelligence somewhat, and in particular ensures you excel in all kinds of theoretical, written, and research-based endeavours. Further, you are more adept with riddles, puzzles, and logic and debating.

With Great Wisdom: The influence of the academic world does not prevent its occupation by fallible and sometimes dishonest people. You have the discernment needed to weigh scholarship according to its true merits, including finding trends of flawed or fraudulent research. You can also articulate these flaws effectively – you are no man’s fool in the arena of ideas.

You have a strong eye for details and a good intuition when it comes to mysteries. This is especially useful when piecing together the many plans of other wizards or when delving into some more esoteric branches of magic. Very useful for those who engage in adventurous pursuits. As a side bonus, you would likely make an excellent seeker in quidditch.

With Great Wisdom: You have an uncanny instinct for the truth, often spotting trickery, deceit, and misinformation at a glance. Even with obscure or conflicting sources, you quickly deduce valuable information, gaining more insight the longer you observe and knowing exactly where to look next. Often, the flaws you expose in an obstacle give you a third approach to a hopeless dilemma.

This perk grants you intuitive understanding of mundane technology at the level of a muggle scientist, engineer, or similar profession. You will also have an easier time learning and understanding this tech. Useful for transfiguration or for adapting muggle technology to work in the wizarding world. Also very useful for blending magic together with technology through enchanting.

With Great Wisdom: Magic is a powerful tool, but for other wizards, it allows the atrophy of mundane problem-solving and reasoning skills. You have an eye for clever, practical solutions to problems. Further, you understand the failings of human reason exposed by muggle psychology, and have applied the lessons to improve your own self-reflection and discipline. Finally, you have a better grasp of the long-term implications of your decisions.

You’re a skilled manipulator, both in personal interactions and among large groups. You can quickly read any social situation and then manoeuvre advantageously – although this skill with social dynamics doesn’t actually make you more likeable. You have a deft talent for politics and a keen danger-sense, knowing just how far you can push things while keeping your hands clean and your neck safe.

With Great Ambition: Your skills with acting, intrigue and spycraft improve. You have an intuitive grasp of how to manipulate through deceit or propaganda, including smearing an opponent or maintaining your own public image. You gain insight into the design of laws and procedures in large organisations, and a keen awareness of how one might exploit them.

You’re a resourceful schemer and skilled implementer of plans, and instinctively grasp the results a particular course of action produces. Your typical long and short-term plans are both very unlikely to fail, and you can manage especially intricate, subtle, or large-scale schemes at greater risk. You’re skilled at using available information to anticipate variables which could endanger your plans, and your talents improve with intelligence, enabling more complex schemes with grander aims.

With Great Ambition: More than a schemer, you’re an efficient and capable strategist. You know how to maintain a plan unnoticed for years, keep it adaptable when dealing with uncertainty, and adjust when the unexpected does arise. Your resourcefulness lets you develop methods of achieving your goals nobody else would consider, entirely evading predicaments that trap others.

You are the best possible combination of your parents. Despite any developmental issues from your background, you’ll usually be the best-looking person in the room, with excellent strength, stamina, disease resistance, and general health. A modest intelligence boost and favourable genetics shore up your other perks, and natural confidence and willpower help you assert yourself and keep moving forward.

With Great Ambition: You were born with a great natural willpower, long-term awareness, and the confidence needed for social dominance and a strong command presence. You resist intimidation and bluster, and are never distracted from what truly matters you. Your determination and focus help you create opportunities and win greater victories, and also prevent you from shrinking from any distasteful or distressing reality.

At little more than a glance you can judge the strength, effectiveness, and corruption of a system, and know how best to improve, exploit, or sabotage it, as you will. You can always recognize injustice. Pairs greatly with Hard Work and Schemes, incorporates other Griffindor perks into itself, strengthens those perks' effects while adding new ones. 

Completion Bonus: You are extremely resilient to trauma, pressure, and mental compulsion, keeping your head where others are overwhelmed or disorientated.  You can overcome the Imperius curse or the most severe trauma without further ill effects, and adapt to extreme states of being like extended lifespan or drastic physiological change without losing your sense of self.

Your ability to form strong mutual bonds is quite incredible. So long as you do your part at least somewhat well, you find that anyone you expect loyalty or service from is inspired to stay loyal and do their best as well. Pairs greatly with Witty, Funny and Cunning, incorporates other Hufflepuff perks into itself, strengthens those perks' effects while adding new ones.

Completion Bonus: You can teach and inspire as you organise a group or direct it to act, soon producing other leaders you can delegate to. Your followers usually come out of trying circumstances stronger, rather than being worn down. You are also effective at instilling some of the mindset and skills from your perks through teaching and inspiration, making allies more capable of acting without your oversight.

You have something even more valuable than knowledge - the ability to use it well. You possess a well-developed common sense, insight and good judgement to apply your skills better. Pairs greatly with Reflexes and Best Match, incorporates other Ravenclaw perks into itself, strengthens those perks' effects while adding new ones.

Completion Bonus: Your efforts to eliminate your cognitive biases have already pushed your mind beyond the human standard, disorienting  legiliments with unusual thought patterns. As a result, your memory is now eidetic, with perfect recall and indexing. Your mind doesn't laze about sticking to trusted patterns, but constantly analyses your memories, searching for new approaches or solutions.

Your ambition acts as a foundation for your sense of self. You know what needs to be done to realize it. You naturally acquire power and know how to efficiently utilize it towards your goals. Pairs greatly with Perceptive and  Charisma, incorporates other Slytherin perks into itself, strengthens those perks' effects while adding new ones.

Completion Bonus: You quickly sense deceit and emotional manipulation, and readily grasp the wider implications of all you observe. Your eye for talent, superior planning skills, and air of competence help you lead and place others advantageously. You excel at gathering information, whether through mundane, obscure data sources or a network of largely unwitting informants.

Magic is often illogical or counterintuitive, but you have an aptitude for even its most esoteric forms. You grasp the nuance of symbolic properties and associations, the strange logic of rituals, or more mysterious concepts like death, sacrifice, love, and time. This is especially invaluable for magic which invokes these primordial, often dangerous forces, in particular powerful rituals, and you know how far you can push such forces without serious risk. You start with instinctive understanding of these obscure topics equivalent to a qualified unspeakable, which is also useful for disciplines like divination, theoretical potions, and even astronomy.

​There is so much more to magic than what these stuffy inbred old purebloods believe, and you can show them! You are an absolute master of the art of Techno-Magic. Making machines that run on magic, or just magical equivalents of Muggle technology, or something as simple as just making muggle devices work in magical environments is all child’s play for you. While you can translate flawlessly between technology and magic, doing something truly revolutionary requires extensive knowledge of both. Fortunately, there’s already a Perk here that can get you started.

Your previous life is fresh in your mind, the memories are distinct but detached. You won't suffer from existential or identity crisis, it's easy to let go of your unfinished business, say farewell to your friends and family and embrace your new life. If you had mental problems or even bad habits, they are gone now if you so wish. On the other hand, you won't suffer from culture shock, raise suspicion due to anachronisms or be confused by muggles because of your pure-blood origin. The new you keeps the best traits of both personalities, decided by your preferences.  The baggage of old life won't drag you down. In case you go through the experience again, from now on this will happen during every type of mind transfer.

You may be the brightest witch or wizard in a generation. Your memory, insight, processing speed, and logical reasoning skills are all vastly improved. What's more, any other perks you took from this section are likely enhanced by this boost in intelligence, making you nearly peerless in your specialties. You additionally gain a talent for languages which allows you to quickly learn dozens of dialects at a time, including more nonsensical languages like Gobbledegook, Mermish, or French. It is worth noting that the intelligence boost from this perk will not help you in learning magic, though it may assist with your creativity, memorization, or innovation of it's use.

With this option you can choose for your appearance to stand out in some way. Glowing eyes or hair, unnatural colours, ect. You can also restrict its manifestations to circumstances like casting, focusing or feeling specific emotions. This is purely cosmetic and cannot be utilised in other way.

Covers any inclination not present in Perks above. If it does exist above, the perks do not stack. This option only gives the talent without any other benefits - things like enhanced memory or reflexes are sold as separate talents. If you already possess a talent naturally, don't waste points buying it here. Can be cooking, kickboxing, driving, chemistry, singing, writing, lying ect ect. A specific field gives more talent than a broad one - like chess vs strategy. This Perk can be bought up for 20 times total, giving talent for different field of your choice each time.

This option also doesn't make you a genius. What it does is provide a learning boost to entry-level skills and knowledge, doubling the speed you learn, internalize and build upon when you begin to study something new. The low-hanging fruits will be easy to pick, building a sturdy foundation for later. Things like biology topics covered in middle school, with the boost petering out at high school material. Anything above entry level will be as difficult to advance in as usual.

You know the Charms subject as well as you would have after studying it yourself for ten years. Includes all school years and independent research. You also have a corresponding degree of skill for someone, who got Outstanding on all their Charms exams. 

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

You know the D.A.D.A subject as well as you would have after studying it yourself for ten years. Includes all school years and independent research. You also have a corresponding degree of skill for someone, who got Outstanding on all their D.A.D.A exams. 

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

You know the Transfiguration subject as well as you would have after studying it yourself for ten years. Includes all school years and independent research. You also have a corresponding degree of skill for someone, who got Outstanding on all their Transfiguration exams. 

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

You know the Potions subject as well as you would have after studying it yourself for ten years. Includes all school years and independent research. You also have a corresponding degree of skill for someone, who got Outstanding on all their Potions exams. 

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

You know the Herbology subject as well as you would have after studying it yourself for ten years. Includes all school years and independent research. You also have a corresponding degree of skill for someone, who got Outstanding on all their Herbology exams. 

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

You know the Care subject as well as you would have after studying it yourself for ten years. Includes all school years and independent research. You also have a corresponding degree of skill for someone, who got Outstanding on all their Care exams. 

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

Gain the full breadth of ten years of education provided by Nicolas Flamel himself, with an occasional lesson from Perenelle. It usually takes talent in several branches to even attempt this field. Without having a gift for alchemy or absurd affinities for potions, transfiguration, chemistry and philosophy, this option won't give you much. If you are one of the few with prospects here, ten years might just be enough to begin studying the great work.

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

You receive ten years in the art of divining information through magic. This could be focused solely on future telling - from tea leaves to oneiromancy to crystal balls to catching echos from the sands of time. It could also be the study of spells, methods and enchantments for getting and organizing actual information, from revelio to library charms to pattern discerning runic matrices to sending queries to the collective unconsciousness of the world.  You have ten years of knowledge in total to allocate between these options.

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

Ten years of studying the magical knowledge of the flesh, in parts vastly outdated or incorrect, while adding the metaphysical aspect missed by the modern medicine, like which organs are responsible for what in magic and mind and soul or how to draw the essense of a lifeform. Covers healing without much experience in the field, transformation spells and rituals like animagery and body enhancement and not much else. Ten years is not nearly enough to be competent here, but even the theory part is invaluable.

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

This branch of magical study covers everything from ghouls and ghosts to infery to poltergeists. A comprehensive guide that allows one to become a real world ghost-buster: spells on how to weaken, banish, capture, exorcise a supernatural, as well as their abilities, weaknesses and habits. Some obscure knowledge here allows the truly gifted or fortunate to call a guardian spirit - from a departed loved one to a totem animal to an amalgamation of the ancestors.  You can choose what topic to focus on, spreading the ten years of study.

Note: It doesn't turn you into a Witch/Wizard.

Typically, accidental magic is just that, it responds to a child's mental state and intense desires, producing feats of magic after reaching a critical point. Few possess enough will and motivation to consistently reenact these mental states to produce accidental magic semi-reliably. For those who do, magic begins to remember those specific feats until they can be performed on demand. However, those parlor tricks aren't wand magic, a structured spell would produce the same result with more depth, power, control and ease.  

It seems, you've been one such child in your early years and accidents just never stopped. Levitating your toys, summoning a bottle, things like these still come easy even after getting a proper wand. You'd still lose these abilities as you grow up unless you practice routinely. If you are eleven or older, choose up to three simple magical effects. If you are five, choose one and retain the ability to learn more.

You have a particular knack for creating entirely new recipes for potions. While most potioneers are capable of this skill, it is often prohibitively expensive and difficult to control the exact effects of what you create. With this you are able to slowly refine your recipes to have whatever effects you are looking to achieve as long as you can afford the ingredients you will need for your many attempts. This process is easier for skilled potioneers and those creating simpler potion effects, as well as those with the scientific knowledge typically used in alchemy. 

Creating new potions can be a profitable, if dangerous business. While not quite as dangerous as spell creation, those who do not employ rigorous safety measures can easily be seriously injured or killed during their experiments.  As a result of this talent in developing potions, you can recollect some points spent on their modifiers.

Perhaps the riskiest and most difficult magical practice of all; you have a talent for inventing new spells. You understand the process involved in doing so, and have a knack for controlling what the spells you create will actually do. This field requires a comprehensive knowledge of the magic type being attempted, and requires users to discover new combinations of incantations, wand movements, and spell theory. This practice can create some truly unique and singularly useful spells, which can even be taught to others. 

Spell creation is extremely dangerous, however. Individuals who experiment too recklessly could end up dead from a single miscast spell attempt, with more powerful spell attempts carrying greater dangers. Only the well prepared should attempt this. As a result of this talent in developing spells, you can recollect some points spent on their modifiers.

With enough magical skill, spells and enchantments can be made to last forever; sometimes even increasing in strength over time. While most who use this style of magic will require high quality enchanting materials or reduced spell effects, you are an exception. By taking this you can cause any spells or enchantments you produce to last forever without having to sacrifice quality. It will also be half as difficult to create enchantments or spell effects that grow in power over time. 

You could inflict curses that grow worse with time, change someone's appearance permanently, or craft magical defenses that will stand the test of time. Spells and enchantments can still be reversed or dispelled by other witches and wizards, and only your enchantments will persist in the event that you are killed.

An advanced technique, most Hogwarts students don't begin to learn non-verbal magic before their sixth year. This is the practice of casting spells without need for verbally saying the incantations aloud. Magic cast in this way is especially useful in magical duels, as users will not telegraph their attacks beforehand. Typically spells cast in this way are less powerful than their spoken counterparts, and require more focus to cast. You have mastered the art of nonverbal magic, and can cast spells you know in this way with little to no extra focus, and at full power. What's more, spells you cast will be less likely to have visual or audio imperfections like loud noises or bright beams of light, and any enchantments or spell effects caused by you are much more difficult for others to detect.

The control you possess over your magic is breath-taking, sometimes literally. It's presence is just beneath the skin and can be coached outwards.
